correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact rim-coordinate model Q_m=conv(e_i,e_i+e_(i+1)) and its inequalities y_i>=0, 1<=sum y<=2 and sum_(i in S)y_i<=1 for independent cycle sets. Dual capacity packing uses fractional vertex-cover vertices (integral covers, plus all-half for odd cycles), proving sufficiency. The metric Gram matrix in rim coordinates is I+J, inverse I-J/(m+1); hence dual norm for j coordinates is sqrt(j(m+1-j)/(m+1)). Group averaging yields a symmetric optimal center. Crossing coordinate and maximal-independent-set margins gives r=1/(ku+v), except m=4 where lower-total versus independent-pair margins give r=1/(u+2v). Equality propagation forces uniqueness except m=4, where both opposite-pair sums are fixed and each member bounded below, producing exactly a rectangle. Facet dimension and contacts were checked against the connected bipartite support-graph rank conditions; m=3 also has upper-total contacts. Independently solved halfspace Chebyshev LP for m=3..11 with agreement; finite LP is not the proof.

value.rationale: The ordinary wheel edge polytope is a canonical graph polytope in the second hypersimplex. Euclidean inradius, all Chebyshev centers and active-facet incidence are natural intrinsic invariants, and the m=4 nonunique two-dimensional locus versus unique centers at all other m is a structural family-wide transition, not a tiny numerical optimization.
